title: adaptive-kernel-ratio-balancer: hybrid INT4/INT8 prefetched kernel path with smooth-scale fusion
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduces a hybrid kernel selector that dynamically packs heads into INT4/INT8 execution lanes and adds a prefetch-aware KV window to reduce hot token stalls. Backwards-compatible: runtime falls back to existing quantized kernels when unsupported configurations are used.
description:
Context & motivation: Production workloads with skewed activation distributions showed suboptimal utilization when pinned to a single quant path (INT8 or FP8). Teams observed that some attention heads are highly amenable to aggressive lowering (INT4/INT8) while others still benefit from higher dynamic range. This PR implements an adaptive kernel ratio balancer that: 1) collects per-head activation histograms during a short warmup window, 2) assigns heads to INT4/INT8 lanes based on a cost model (accuracy delta vs. throughput gain), and 3) emits fused dequantization/smooth-scaling wrappers so the execution path amortizes dequant overheads. Additionally, a small KV prefetch window coordinator was added to shadow-copy likely-needed KV slices into a low-latency buffer while the balancer is deciding head placement, reducing head-switch stalls during continuous batching.

What changed (high level): - New adaptive balancer module (runtime/kernel/ratio_balancer.{cc,h}) that computes a lightweight head-score and packing plan. - Head packer that groups heads into lanes to maximize vector utilization (runtime/kernel/head_packer.*). - Hybrid execution shim (runtime/kernel/hybrid_exec_shim.cc) that dispatches to INT4 microkernels for packed lanes and INT8 microkernels for others. - Fused smooth-scale + dequant pass in the runtime graph emitter (compiler/passes/fuse_smooth_dequant.cpp). - Prefetch coordinator that maintains a small LRU shadow buffer for KV cache slices (runtime/kv/prefetch_window.*). - Tests and benchmarks (tests/perf/hybrid_balancer_perf.py, tests/unit/ratio_balancer_test.cc).

Benchmark summary (on n1-standard equivalent, A100-40GB profile): - Baseline (int8-only path): p50 token latency 12.4ms, p95 28.7ms, throughput 132 tokens/s per GPU. - Hybrid balancer (warmup 64 requests): p50 10.1ms (-18.5%), p95 23.9ms (-16.7%), throughput 174 tokens/s (+31.8%). - Cost model ablation (no prefetch): throughput +18% (shows prefetch contributes ~13% uplift on hot-key workloads). - Quality impact: average per-token logprobs changed by -0.0009 on internal eval set; no statistically significant token-level regressions observed in 10k prompt validation.

Implementation notes: - The balancer runs as an inexpensive background pass during the first N continuous-batched windows (configurable, default N=64). It samples activations (per-head RMS) and computes a head score. - Packing heuristics favor coalescing contiguous heads (cache locality) and attempt to keep lanes at or near preferred vector width for the microkernels. - The hybrid_exec_shim performs a zero-copy switch where possible; when lane formats differ, an in-place fused dequant+scale operation is emitted to minimize memory churn. - Prefetch window keeps up to 8 recent KV segments per active stream; window size is tunable via agent config.

Compatibility & rollout: - Fallthroughs: if model architecture is unsupported (e.g., non-standard head layout) the balancer remains disabled and the runtime uses the default INT8 path. - Feature flag: runtime flag "adaptive_kernel_ratio" (off by default for Hosted) and opt-in via Dedicated/Private configs. - Canary: plan to roll to 5% traffic for two days then 25% for a week, monitor token-level quality regressions and tail latency.

Tests & CI: - Unit tests for head packing and cost-model logic. - Microbenchmark harness added to perf suite; CI runs a smoke perf measurement on synthetic inputs. - All checks passed in CI (linux-build, unit, perf-smoke).

Commit summary: [c7b4a9d] introduce ratio_balancer core and head scoring logic; [a1d3b2c] head_packer and lane allocator; [f5e2b3a] hybrid_exec_shim and microkernel hooks (int4/int8); [d6a9f1b] fuse smoothscale + dequant pass; [e2c8b7a] KV prefetch window and config; [b3c2a1f] perf tests and docs.

Files changed (high-level): - runtime/kernel/ratio_balancer.cc/h - runtime/kernel/head_packer.cc/h - runtime/kernel/hybrid_exec_shim.cc - compiler/passes/fuse_smooth_dequant.cpp - runtime/kv/prefetch_window.{cc,h} - tests/perf/hybrid_balancer_perf.py - tests/unit/ratio_balancer_test.cc - docs/observability/adaptive_kernel.md

Review conversation: Ethan Zhao: "Nice direction — two quick asks: (1) can we expose a debug endpoint that prints the current head packing plan per-stream? (2) the cost model constants look magic, please source them or add comments." Priya Nair (author): "Added a /debug/packing endpoint guarded by experimental flags and added comments explaining derivation; constants moved to a tunable table (now documented)." Mariana Lopez: "Can you add a short test that exercises an unsupported layout so we validate the fallthrough?" Priya: "Added ratio_balancer_unsupported_layout test; CI covers it." Oliver Chen (LGTM): "Observed the perf boost in local perf harness. Approving after CI green."

CI & merge: - linux-build: pass - unit: pass - perf-smoke: pass - integration: pass - flake/lint: pass

Merge method: squash and merge.

Risks & mitigations: - Risk: small accuracy regressions for some edge-case layers. Mitigation: default-off for Hosted, gradual rollout, and automatic rollback on quality regression alerts. - Risk: increased memory pressure from prefetch window. Mitigation: window size tuned with upper bound and LRU eviction.

Follow-ups: - Wire head-level tracing into Console for per-route packing visibility (ENG-12920). - Explore adding a short per-head quant-aware calibration step during model upload to eliminate the warmup sample period.

Related work: references several internal perf PRs and the quant kernel optimizer RFC (ENG-11890).
